title: Local separating pencils with prescribed unramified fibres
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme, $K=k(S)$, and $f:X\to S$ an H-projective morphism with $X$ integral of finite type over $k$. Assume all geometric fibres are pure of dimension one and the generic fibre $C=X_K$ is smooth and geometrically integral. Let $M\subset C$ be a reduced finite etale closed subscheme. Let $J$ be a finite group acting on $X$ over $S$ and preserving $M$ (thus fixing $K$ pointwise). There is a finite separable extension $E/K$ with the following property. Write $S_E$ for the normalization of $S$ in $E$ and $X_E$ for the normalization of $X$ in the compositum $k(X)E$; the latter compositum is the fraction field of $k(X)\otimes_K E$. The action of $J$ extends by acting trivially on $E$. There is a finite affine open covering $S_E=\bigcup_{i=1}^rU_i$ and finite surjective $U_i$-morphisms $\varphi_i:(X_E)_{U_i}\to\mathbf P^1_{U_i}$ invariant under $J$. On the generic curve $C_E$, each $\varphi_i$ is generically etale, and the inverse image of $\{0,1,\infty\}$ is a reduced finite etale $E$-scheme disjoint from $M_E$. The finite-etale fibre condition is equivalently that $\varphi_i$ is etale at all points above these three values; disjointness from $M_E$ is an additional requirement. If $\dim S>0$, one may take $E=K$. If $S$ is zero dimensional, $S_E=\operatorname{Spec}E$, one open suffices, and $X_E=C_E$.

The notions used are [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-projective], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-fin-normalization-extension], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-pure-dimension], [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. A finite separable extension is a finite-dimensional field extension whose elements have separable minimal polynomials. Group actions on schemes and fields may be nonfaithful and semilinear on the ground field.

proof.text: Apply the normal-model lemma with $E=K$, $L=k(X)$ to obtain $\nu:N\to X$, with $N/S$ H-projective, pure one-dimensional geometric fibres and generic fibre $C$; it extends the $J$-action. Normality identifies $S_K=S$. Projectivity makes $N/S$ proper, so its closed image containing the generic point is all of $S$. Both schemes are Noetherian, being finite type over $k$.

source.place: de Jong §§3.3--3.5, pp.605--606; short assembly of the quotient-free norm-section arguments extracted by O2

proof.text: Use the effective-action norm lemma: $G=\operatorname{im}(J\to\operatorname{Aut}_S(N))$ acts faithfully on $C$. Choose an H-projective embedding and its $L=i^*\mathcal O(1)$. On every affine base open this $L$ and its fibre restrictions are ample. The orbit bundle and its norm sections give $J$-invariant pencils and commute with fibres and powers.

source.place: de Jong §§3.3--3.5, pp.605--606; short assembly of the quotient-free norm-section arguments extracted by O2

proof.text: If $\dim S>0$, each closed point $s$ has an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with nonzero maximal ideal: otherwise $s$ would be the closed generic point and $S$ a point. Apply relative norm-pair interpolation to obtain ordinary sections whose norm pairs give a finite pencil on $N_s$ and a finite surjective generically etale pencil on $C$.

source.place: de Jong §§3.3--3.5, pp.605--606; short assembly of the quotient-free norm-section arguments extracted by O2

proof.text: Apply finite shrinking to the norm pair, obtaining an invariant finite surjection $\psi:N_U\to\mathbf P^1_U$. The domain $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ is infinite since its maximal ideal is nonzero. Integral coordinate avoidance applied to $\psi,C,M$ gives $\varphi=g\circ\psi$ with the required three reduced finite etale fibres disjoint from $M$.

source.place: de Jong §§3.3--3.5, pp.605--606; short assembly of the quotient-free norm-section arguments extracted by O2

proof.text: These affine neighbourhoods of all closed points cover $S$: a nonempty closed complement has a minimal nonempty closed subset by Noetherianity, a singleton since schemes are $T_0$, hence a closed point. Quasi-compactness supplies a finite subcover. With $E=K$ the normal-model identification gives $X_E=N$ and $S_E=S$.

source.place: de Jong §§3.3--3.5, pp.605--606; short assembly of the quotient-free norm-section arguments extracted by O2

proof.text: If $\dim S=0$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$: its sole point is generic, an affine neighbourhood is all of $S$, and its reduced zero-dimensional domain is a field. Thus $X=C$ is smooth and normal. Choose an embedding and its ample $L$. For the effective $G$, the separating-pair theorem supplies $n$ and a nonempty open $W_n$ of ordinary section pairs, with finite-dimensional section space and the stated norm-pencil properties over every extension field.

source.place: de Jong §§3.3--3.5, pp.605--606; short assembly of the quotient-free norm-section arguments extracted by O2

proof.text: Apply finite separable open-pencil specialization to $C,G,L,n,W_n,M$, obtaining $E/K$, the ordinary pair and its avoiding coordinate matrix. This gives every pencil and marked-fibre condition over $E$. The scalar-extension clause of the normal-model lemma identifies $S_E=\operatorname{Spec}E$ and $X_E=C_E$, and extends $J$ by fixing $E$. One affine open suffices.
